# Continual-ARC task task-16ce026f — slide object toward barrier and mark trailing edge

## Inferred rule (verified on test)
A monochrome foreground shape is placed on a uniform background, with a straight full-width/full-height color-2 barrier. Slide the foreground shape in the direction of the barrier until it is immediately adjacent to the barrier (preserve its shape and color). Then draw a full grid-spanning line of color 8 immediately beyond the shape's far edge, on the side opposite the barrier. The barrier and other background remain unchanged. In demos, the movement distance varies, and the shape translates without changing its internal pattern. If it is already adjacent to the barrier, it does not move; draw the color-8 line just outside its opposite extreme edge.

## Evidence from demos
- Demo 1: vertical color-2 barrier near right edge; color-7 object slides right one cell to become adjacent; output adds full-height color-8 line at the object's left/trailing side.
- Demo 2: horizontal barrier below object; object shifts down one cell until adjacent; adds full-width color-8 line above its new top edge.
- Demo 3: horizontal barrier above object; object shifts up until adjacent; adds full-width color-8 line below its new bottom edge.
- Demo 4: object is already immediately above horizontal barrier; it stays put and a full-width color-8 line is added just above it.
- Demo 5: vertical barrier left of object; object shifts left to become adjacent; adds full-height color-8 line just to the right of its final rightmost edge.

## Test result
The test had background 3, foreground 5 and a horizontal color-2 barrier at row 21 (0-based). The foreground shape was already directly above/touching the barrier, so it remained unchanged. Added color 8 across the entire width at row 11, immediately above its topmost row (12). This submission was confirmed CORRECT.

## Pitfalls
- Do not color the object's far-edge row; place the 8-line just outside the final translated shape.
- Do not infer the direction from the apparent majority of foreground cells; use the color-2 barrier.
- Preserve all existing cells, including holes, disconnected same-color specks, and background around the object; only translate foreground toward the barrier and add the full-span 8-line.
- Use zero-based grid indexing when generating the line coordinate.

## Additional verified instance (2026-09-30)
This stream instance confirms the rule for a vertical barrier and both an already-adjacent and translating shape:
- Demo 1: 30x29, background 9, barrier color 2 at column 12; color-6 shape was already immediately to its right (starting at column 13). It stayed in place and output added color 8 down the full grid height at column 15, just beyond the shape's far/right edge.
- Demo 2: 17x19, background 4, barrier color 2 at column 14; irregular color-5 shape lay to its left with a two-column gap. It translated right by 2 columns until its rightmost edge was at column 13, adjacent to the barrier, then added color 8 down the full height at column 7, just beyond the translated shape's leftmost edge.
- Test: 20x19, background 9, barrier at column 13; irregular color-7 shape occupied rows 9-17 and columns 1-4, with rightmost edge initially 9 columns left of the barrier. It translated right by 8 columns, placing its rightmost edge at column 12, immediately adjacent to the barrier. The correct output preserves the pattern at rows 9-17, columns 9-12 and adds a full-height color-8 line at column 8 (one column beyond the translated shape's leftmost edge). This was confirmed CORRECT.
- Useful calculation: for a vertical barrier at column `b` and object edge on its left at `rmax`, translate by `b - 1 - rmax`; put the full-height 8-line at translated `cmin - 1`. If the object is on the barrier's right, translate left until `cmin = b + 1`, then put the line at `cmax + 1`. For horizontal barriers, apply the analogous row formulas.
- Avoid the tempting but incorrect shortcut of putting the 8-line at the grid's outermost column: it marks the object's trailing edge, not the canvas edge.

## Further verified instance (2026-09-30)
- Test: 16x11, background 3; full-width color-2 barrier at row 10; color-5 L/tromino at `(13,5), (14,6), (14,7)` (zero-based). It moved up 2 rows to `(11,5), (12,6), (12,7)`, making its topmost row immediately adjacent to the barrier, and color 8 was placed across the full width at row 13 (one row past the translated shape's bottom edge). This output was confirmed CORRECT.
- Two demos showed that the barrier may be vertical or horizontal and can occur on either side of the shape: translate the foreground straight toward the barrier until adjacent, preserving its exact pattern, then put the perpendicular full-span color-8 line one cell beyond the far edge opposite the barrier. A demo with vertical barrier at column 26 and object on its left had the shape move right until adjacent; 8-line at column 21, beyond its trailing side. Thus barrier need not be at canvas edge.
